newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Renison sees financing as growth push.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Renison sees financing as growth push.

text.p: RGC Ltd said a $US375 million refinancing programme announced on Tuesday would allow for more flexibility in acquiring new assets or expanding existing ones.
RGC said the programme consisted of a $250 million five-year revolving credit facility and a $125 million three-year revolving credit facility.

"We have sufficient room to move within these facilities to make some further acquisitions partly with debt or fully with debt depending on the size," Peter Housden, RGC's executive director of finance, told Reuters.
Housden would not name any potential targets but said RGC was on the lookout for new opportunities within its existing areas of operation, which include mineral sands and base metals.
"We'd do it either through joint ventures, through exploration, through acquisitions," Housden said.

RGC recently completed a takeover bid giving it 76.7 percent of minerals sand group Cudgen RZ Ltd and has said it sees pockets of growth in markets for minerals sands, particularly zircon and to a lesser extent titianium dioxide.
RGC is 40 percent-owned by British conglomerate Hanson Plc and is one of the world's biggest mineral sands miners.

However, its ability to exploit market conditions have been dampended to some extent by its Sierra Leone rutile mining operations, which have been suspended since January 1995 due to a rebel insurgency.
RGC also has shown an interest in expanding tin-producing operations beyond Australia and Indonesia, which together should account for about 10 percent of world tin production in 1996/97.
One direction could be Latin America where RGC is one of three companies on a short list to buy the tin assets of Bolivian state-owned mining group COMIBOL, including a tin smelter and two mines.
"We're looking at all of these areas for opportunities," Housden said.

Housden said the refinancing was separate from any financing of its Goldfields Ltd subsidiary, which was established last year as a purely gold mining company, combining the gold assets of RGC and Pancontinental Mining Ltd.
